review_notes: I read the whole file and the downstream uses of the three simp-tagged iff lemmas. I found them only in ComplexPlaces.lean and RankOne.lean, and every use is an explicit `rw [...]` with the nondegeneracy proofs supplied. A grep of the QuadraticForm directory found no simp lemmas or tagged declarations that would discharge `Q.Nondegenerate` side goals. I did not search Mathlib for such simp lemmas. I could not run Lean, so I do not claim any observed simp behaviour. My claim that simp would fail to discharge the hypotheses is therefore an inference. The private `isometryEquivSumSquaresUnits` and the theorem `not_anisotropic_of_isSepClosed` have no simp-interface problems.

findings.problem: Both iff lemmas are `@[simp]`, and both are conditional on `Nondegenerate` hypotheses. They overlap on goals of the form `Q.Equivalent (weightedSumSquares K (1 : Fin n → K))`. The general lemma needs `hQ` and `hR`. The specialised lemma needs only `hQ`. Simp has no canonical way to prefer one, and the general lemma's side goal about `weightedSumSquares K 1` is an unnecessary extra obligation. Neither side condition is something simp can discharge. A grep of the QuadraticForm directory shows no simp-tagged Nondegenerate lemmas, and I did not check Mathlib for such lemmas. So the attributes give little automation. They only add two overlapping, hypothesis-guarded rewrite rules to the global simp set.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `equivalent_iff_finrank_eq_of_isSepClosed`. If one of the two is to stay a simp lemma, keep only the specialised `equivalent_weightedSumSquares_one_iff_finrank_eq`, whose normal form is `finrank = n` and which has a single hypothesis. Otherwise remove both. Callers can keep using `rw`, as they do now.
findings.benefit: This removes competing conditional rules on the same LHS shape. It also makes the simp set predictable, so a failed side-condition discharge in one lemma cannot hide the other.

findings.problem: This lemma is tagged `@[simp]`, but it is guarded by two `Nondegenerate` hypotheses. It rewrites the general predicate `Q.IsRepresentedBy R` into a dimension inequality. Simp cannot be expected to prove `Q.Nondegenerate` and `R.Nondegenerate` for arbitrary forms. The only observed use is an explicit `rw` that passes both proofs. The attribute therefore adds a global rewrite for `IsRepresentedBy` over any sep-closed field that will rarely fire. When it does fire, it silently replaces a structural predicate with a numeric inequality, but only if the hypotheses happen to be dischargeable.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `isRepresentedBy_iff_finrank_le_of_isSepClosed`. It can be used by explicit `rw` or `simp [isRepresentedBy_iff_finrank_le_of_isSepClosed, hQ, hR]` when wanted. A simp lemma is only warranted if a simp-set for `Nondegenerate` is added alongside it.
findings.benefit: Users of `IsRepresentedBy` keep a stable simp normal form. The unusable conditional rule no longer sits in the default simp set. The file's simp interface then lists only rewrites that can actually fire.
